Here's the full plan for your Stocks Portfolio Tracker:

---

## Stocks Portfolio Tracker — Implementation Plan

### Requirements Restatement
- Multi-user stocks portfolio tracker
- Vue 3 + Vite + PWA + Pinia + PrimeVue (JS, no TS)
- Node.js backend with MongoDB (encrypted at rest)
- Yahoo Finance scraping / free API for price data
- Periodic price polling (not WebSocket)
- D3.js for data visualizations

---

### Architecture Overview

```
Frontend (Vue 3 + Vite)          Backend (Node.js + Express)
├── PrimeVue UI components   ←→  ├── REST API
├── Pinia stores                 ├── Auth (JWT)
├── D3 charts                    ├── MongoDB (Mongoose)
└── PWA (offline shell)          ├── Yahoo Finance scraper
                                 └── Cron polling job
```

---

### Phase 1 — Project Scaffold
- Vite + Vue 3 project (JS)
- PrimeVue + PrimeIcons setup
- Pinia store setup
- Vue Router with route guards
- PWA plugin (`vite-plugin-pwa`) — manifest + service worker
- Node.js/Express API with folder structure
- MongoDB connection via Mongoose
- `.env` config for both client + server

---

### Phase 2 — Auth (Multi-user)
- User model (email, hashed password, created)
- Register / Login endpoints (bcrypt + JWT)
- Auth middleware for protected routes
- Pinia `authStore` — token, user, login/logout
- Login + Register pages (PrimeVue forms)
- Route guards on Vue Router

---

### Phase 3 — Portfolio Data Model
MongoDB collections:
- `users` — auth
- `portfolios` — one per user, holds positions
- `positions` — ticker, shares, avg cost, user ref
- `transactions` — buy/sell log (ticker, type, price, shares, date)
- `watchlist` — tickers per user

---

### Phase 4 — Yahoo Finance Integration
- `yahoo-finance2` npm package (maintained, free, no key needed)
- Backend service: `stockService.js`
  - `getQuote(ticker)` — current price, change, %change, volume
  - `getHistory(ticker, range)` — OHLCV data for charts
- Cron job (`node-cron`) — poll prices every 5 min for all active tickers
- Cache quotes in MongoDB or in-memory (avoid hammering Yahoo)

---

### Phase 5 — Core API Endpoints
```
POST   /api/auth/register
POST   /api/auth/login

GET    /api/portfolio              — holdings + current values
POST   /api/portfolio/transaction  — buy/sell
DELETE /api/portfolio/position/:id

GET    /api/stocks/quote/:ticker
GET    /api/stocks/history/:ticker?range=1mo

GET    /api/watchlist
POST   /api/watchlist
DELETE /api/watchlist/:ticker
```

---

### Phase 6 — Frontend Views
| View | Components |
|---|---|
| Dashboard | Total value card, day P&L, top movers, allocation donut (D3) |
| Holdings | PrimeVue DataTable, sortable, P&L per position |
| Stock Detail | D3 line/area chart, quote stats, buy/sell modal |
| Transactions | PrimeVue DataTable with filters |
| Watchlist | Card grid, quick-add to portfolio |
| Auth | Login / Register forms |

---

### Phase 7 — D3 Visualizations
- **Portfolio allocation** — donut chart (by ticker or sector)
- **Portfolio value over time** — area chart (based on transaction history)
- **Stock price history** — line chart on Stock Detail page
- **Day gainers/losers** — horizontal bar chart on Dashboard

---

### Phase 8 — PWA
- App manifest (name, icons, theme color)
- Service worker — cache app shell, offline fallback page
- Install prompt handling

---

### Risks

| Risk | Level | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Yahoo Finance scraping breaks | MEDIUM | `yahoo-finance2` is actively maintained; fallback to Alpha Vantage free tier |
| MongoDB encryption at rest | LOW | Use MongoDB Atlas with encryption-at-rest enabled (free tier supports it) |
| JWT token security | MEDIUM | Short expiry + refresh token or httpOnly cookie |
| D3 + Vue reactivity conflicts | LOW | Wrap D3 in Vue `onMounted` / `watch`, use refs for containers |
| Rate limiting on Yahoo | MEDIUM | Cache aggressively, poll only active tickers |

---

### Folder Structure (proposed)
```
/client        ← Vite + Vue
  /src
    /components
    /views
    /stores      ← Pinia
    /composables
    /charts      ← D3 modules
    /router

/server        ← Node.js + Express
  /routes
  /controllers
  /models       ← Mongoose
  /services     ← stockService, cronJobs
  /middleware   ← auth
```

---

**Does this plan look right?** Anything to add, drop, or reorder before we start building?

Some decisions to confirm:
- MongoDB **Atlas** (cloud, free tier) or **local** instance?
- JWT in **httpOnly cookie** or **localStorage** (cookie is safer)?
- D3 chart priority — which one first?
